entrypoints.summary: A Scala compiler service processes an untrusted, maliciously crafted TASTy file containing unexpected negative offsets; ordinary local or CI compilation is explicitly distinguished from this exposure model.

affected_components.role: Post-fix reader context: readEnd derives an end from readNat plus current position, goto changes the byte position, and until iterates while the position is below the end.

code_slices.fixed: The post-fix snapshot exposes readEnd, goto, and until as relevant parser primitives; the reviewed PR describes added Nat/LongNat negativity and integer-overflow checks.
code_slices.surrounding_context: readEnd forms an absolute end from readNat plus bp, goto assigns bp from an address, and until continues while bp is less than the end index.
code_slices.vulnerable: Pre-fix source/diff is not included; vulnerable implementation details are represented only by report and PR descriptions.

negative_controls: A valid TASTy file should parse with forward-moving section boundaries.
A malformed invalid end should be rejected after remediation rather than processed indefinitely.
observability.positive_marker: Infinite loop or nontermination during TastyUnpickler section loading.

preconditions: Scala compiler is deployed as a service or otherwise processes untrusted TASTy input.
Attacker can submit a maliciously crafted TASTy file.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Malformed variable-length TASTy integer / section-end encoding.
trigger_steps.summary: Submit a TASTy artifact containing a variable-length encoded value that yields an unexpected negative offset or invalid section end.

mitigations.concept: Reject invalid decoded TASTy integers and non-forward section ends

relation_candidates.rationale: A malicious TASTy file with an unexpected negative offset reaches the compiler's TASTy parsing path and violates its section-boundary assumptions.
relation_candidates.src: Untrusted TASTy artifact supplied to a compiler service

relation_candidates.rationale: Bad section ends can move parsing backward, and the reported result is an infinite loop during section loading.
The maintainer publication characterizes the relevant untrusted-service exposure as potentially causing denial-of-service-type behavior.

relation_candidates.dst: Reject invalid decoded TASTy integers and non-forward section ends
relation_candidates.rationale: The reviewed PR adds checks against negative Nat/LongNat reads and integer overflow; the audit calls for rejection of overlong encodings and section ends not strictly ahead of the current position.

sources.concept: Untrusted TASTy artifact supplied to a compiler service

impact.attacker_capability: Cause a compiler service that processes attacker-supplied TASTy input to remain in nonterminating section parsing.
impact.security_effect: Denial of service through infinite looping while loading sections from a malicious TASTy file.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker supplies a crafted TASTy artifact to a compiler deployment that accepts untrusted input.
Encoded variable-length TASTy integer data can yield a negative offset/section end when parser fields are not constrained to nonnegative, non-overflowing natural-number values.
Section loading accepts a bad end that can move parsing backward rather than strictly forward, so TastyUnpickler section processing fails to make progress and loops indefinitely.
Nontermination during hostile TASTy parsing can consume compiler-service processing capacity, producing denial-of-service-type behavior.

failure.operation: TastyUnpickler section loading loops without progress after accepting a malformed section end.

primary_invariant.kind: parser progress and natural-number section-boundary validity
primary_invariant.statement: A decoded TASTy Nat/LongNat used for a section end must be nonnegative and non-overflowing, and the resulting end address must be strictly ahead of the current parser position before repositioning or iterating over the section.
primary_invariant.violated_because: Malformed variable-length integer input was allowed to decode to an unexpected negative offset/invalid section end, permitting a section end to move parsing backward.

quality.review_notes: The primary audit, maintainer publication, and merged PR agree on hostile TASTy input, negative offsets/bad ends, infinite looping, and generalized numeric validation. The PR reports a new test, but its body, fixture, execution output, immutable final diff, and exact malicious byte sequence are absent from this bundle; the unit-test oracle is therefore a contract rather than evidence of a passing run. The provided source snapshot is post-fix context and is not treated as proof of pre-fix behavior.

remediation.invariant_restored: Nat and LongNat reads reject negative decoded values, integer reads reject overflow, and malformed section ends cannot move parser position backward; the audit additionally specifies that readEnd must require a computed end strictly greater than the current position before goto.

state_context.attacker_state_setup: Provide a TASTy artifact whose encoded integer produces an invalid negative offset or bad section end.
data_structure_invariants: Decoded Nat/LongNat values must not be negative.
Computed section end must be strictly ahead of the current byte position.
Section parsing must make forward progress toward its end.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: Attacker controls encoded values only when a compiler service accepts an untrusted TASTy artifact.
numeric_domains.name: TASTy Nat/LongNat section length or offset
sentinel_values: end address not strictly greater than current position
numeric_domains.width: variable-length encoded integer; audit notes an Int-fitting value requires at most five 7-bit groups

state_context.state_machine: TASTy section loading derives a section end from a variable-length integer, uses it as a parser boundary, and iterates while parser position remains before that boundary.

oracle.expected_negative: Valid TASTy input continues to parse with valid forward section boundaries.
oracle.expected_positive: Malformed TASTy integer or section-end input is rejected rather than allowing section loading to run indefinitely.
